# Print

> Proof of humanity, aggregated. One SDK over every proof-of-humanity protocol,
> scored by what an adversary would actually pay to fake it. Scores are computed
> client-side against live chains; the on-chain registry stores protocols, never people.

Print answers "is there a human behind this address, and what would faking that
cost?" It reads World ID (Orb, via AgentBook on World Chain), Proof of Humanity v2 and
Circles v2 (Gnosis), and Coinbase Verifications (EAS on Base) — permissionlessly, no
vendor API on the critical path. Scoring rule: saturate within a trust root, sum across
roots; each credential priced at min(forge_cost, rent_cost), age-weighted (Decay for
liveness/KYC, survival Ramp for vouching registries). Every result carries caveats,
including the permanent `independent-control-not-attested`. `isHuman(threshold)` throws
unless the caller chooses an explicit threshold.

## For agents

- MCP server: `npx -y @printid/mcp` — tools: lookup_personhood, check_personhood,
  explain_trust_roots, explain_weight_history
- SDK: `npm install @printid/sdk` — `new Print().resolve('name.eth')`
- Registry (Sepolia): 0x977b028b900cce8ee89c46877e814eff3060aa07 — adapters, trust roots,
  forge/rent costs in cents, age curves; every weight change is an auditable event
- Protocol subgraph: https://api.studio.thegraph.com/query/77602/poh/version/latest
- Weight audit trail: REGISTRY_SUBGRAPH_URL_TBD

## Pages

- / : landing with a live lookup ledger (real RPC probes, threshold slider, full evidence)
- /app.html : the console — full workbench with the additive-vs-root-cost comparison

Built at ETHGlobal Lisbon 2026. Weights are dated, sourced human judgments — not
measurements — and live on-chain with their sources.
